speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: asked the Minister for Manpower whether foreign workers in Singapore have been informed of (i) the available channels to seek recourse against their employers who failed to pay their salaries and (ii) the law against illegal assembly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The education of MWs does not stop at the SIP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: MWs with salary arrears may also approach the Forward Assurance and Support Team (FAST) officers or Friends of ACE (FACE).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Or they can also inform MOM through the monthly salary survey on the FWMOMCare app.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The majority of MWs are registered users of the app.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Unions and NGOs, such as the Migrant Workers’ Centre which operates a hotline, are another source of support for MWs and can advise MWs on the avenues of help and work with MOM to render the necessary assistance to MWs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The number of salary claims filed by MWs has come down significantly in recent years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Nonetheless, we recognise the importance of timely payment of salaries to all workers and we will continue our efforts to arrest salary arrears early and assist all workers, both local and foreign, to promptly recover their owed salaries.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Whilst I am sympathetic towards their concern, may I ask the Senior Minister of State whether MOM would be working with MHA to take action against companies that fail to pay the salaries and also the workers who choose to take the law into their own hands and make public protests?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Would MOM be working with the Police to prosecute such workers?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I gather that the Member is referring to the recent incident on 18 October 2022.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Specific to the incident, I am unable to give too much detail as the Police investigations are still ongoing.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: What I will say is this: pertaining to salary claims, we take a very strong view and a strong principle that when a worker is owed salary, he must be paid.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The other five and the rest of the employees in Zhengda Corporation actually have no salary claims.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: They are all okay and they were not owed any salary payments.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, to a certain extent, that is good.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For those who were owed salary payments, we have assisted them to settle all the payments.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, that has been settled, once they come to MOM and we tried to mediate.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But, in fact, we go one step further.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, we moved upstream and found out about that and we have been assisting the workers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, it is not that the employer had deliberately held back the payments but we understand that during these challenging times, sometimes, payments are delayed.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I think we all know the challenges the construction sector is facing.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, we try to mediate and see how we can best come to a middle ground and settle.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: If we push too hard, the company folds and it is not good for the workers, too.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Rest assured that most of the payments have already been paid.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The owed salaries are partially settled; and we are now settling the rest and there is an instalment plan being worked out.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For public order, MHA is fully apprised of the incident and is doing investigations and will take appropriate actions if necessary.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One way forward, in terms of this salary dispute, is to ensure that MWs are paid electronically.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I ask the Senior Minister of State for an update on what percentage of MWs are now paid electronically and whether we can completely fill the gap and make it 100%?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Today, I would say that almost all employers are already doing so.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, I think we have made that improvement in the last couple of years.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Among the small minority of employers who have yet to switch, some indicated administrative issues, while others cited workers' preference for receiving salary in cash.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But I would say this, that almost all are now on electronic payment.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, we have made that progress and I just want to thank all the employers for working with us on this.
